intro: An AI assistant for HR generalists on a Mac should help with the work on your screen, not take it over. Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in the notch. Hold Option and Command to ask about anything on screen, and it answers out loud and points at what you need.
tldr: Most of an HR generalist's day goes to email, paperwork, and small requests that arrive all at once.
Hold Option and Command to ask about what is on screen. Lazur answers out loud and points at things.
Hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor in any app. Lazur drafts text, but you read it and send it.
Lazur does not click buttons or operate apps for you. You keep control of every sent message and every change.
Check your employer's rules before you put employee records into any AI tool.

blocks.text: Where an HR generalist's day goes

The Bureau of Labor Statistics describes HR specialists as the people who hire, onboard, and keep records. Their listed duties include interviewing applicants, checking references, running orientation, and processing paperwork. The same list says specialists sometimes manage benefits and payroll. The BLS page does not mention software. Most of that work still happens on a screen.

items: Hiring: consult with employers on needs, interview applicants, check references and backgrounds
Offers and onboarding: inform applicants about job details, hire or refer, run new-employee orientation
Records: keep employment records and process paperwork
Pay and benefits: sometimes manage benefits administration and payroll processing

blocks.text: Email is the part most people underestimate. Microsoft's 2023 Work Trend Index surveyed 31,000 full-time workers in 31 markets. Its usage data came from Microsoft 365 activity over 28 days. Microsoft found the average employee spends 57% of their time communicating in meetings, email, and chat. Email is 15% of that split.

Those are workforce numbers, not HR numbers. The research does not measure how much time HR generalists spend in email. The heaviest 25% of email users spend 8.8 hours a week on it. That is more than a full eight-hour day. If your inbox sits in that top quarter, email is most of your job.

Workload is the second problem. SHRM's 2025 State of the Workplace, covered by HR Dive, found that 62% of HR professionals worked beyond their capacity in the prior year. Another 57% said their department was understaffed. When one person covers hiring, records, and payroll questions, small tasks get pushed to the end of the day.

blocks.title: Read the 8.8 hours carefully
blocks.text: The 8.8 hour figure covers the heaviest 25% of Microsoft 365 email users in 2023. It is not a measure of HR work. Use it as a signal to track your own week, not as a target.
How much of the day is admin work

A 2018 survey by West Monroe asked 500 US managers how many hours a day they spend on admin tasks. 36% said 3 to 4 hours. Another 23% said 5 or more. These respondents were managers, not HR staff. Treat the survey as a rough proxy for admin load, not a measure of your week.

Some blogs quote higher admin shares for HR. I could not trace those figures to a primary source, so this page leaves them out. Your own numbers will tell you more than any average. Keep a simple log for five working days.

Write each task on its own row and note the minutes it took. Use plain labels such as email replies, paperwork, spreadsheet fixes, and questions from managers. After a week, two rows will usually stand out. Those are the first tasks to hand to an assistant.
What an AI assistant for HR generalists does on your Mac

Lazur gives you seven kinds of help, and each one fits a different part of the day. Explain answers a question about what is on screen. Point circles where something is and labels it. Guide walks you through a task one click at a time, waiting for each click. Dictate types clean, formatted text at the cursor. Draft writes text you can edit. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs and returns a summary and a report. Everyday covers timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, and opening apps.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. You stay in control of every click and every sent message. That limit is useful. The assistant guides your hands, and the work stays yours.
Hold Option and Command to ask about anything on screen. Hold fn to dictate. Those two keys cover most of a generalist's questions. The table shows how common requests map to what comes back.

blocks.text: Email: drafting replies that still sound like you

Email is where an assistant saves the most minutes, but only if you give it the facts. Keep the thread open in Gmail or Outlook for Mac. Hold Option and Command, then say what the reply must do. Lazur reads the thread on screen and drafts a reply. You read it, change the tone, and press Send yourself.
Name the decision, the deadline, and the tone. Reply to this is vague. Decline the leave politely, ask for the note by Friday, and keep it under five sentences gives Lazur something to work with.

items: Open the thread so the full message is on screen.
Hold Option and Command and state the goal: decline, ask for documents, or confirm a date.
Ask for a shorter or warmer version if the first draft reads stiff.
Hold fn in the reply box to dictate details you want kept exact.
Check names, dates, and amounts against the source before you press Send.

blocks.text: Outlook for Mac: the new client and the legacy client

Outlook for Mac now has two clients. To switch to the new client, open Outlook and turn off the Legacy Outlook switch. To go back, choose Help > Revert to Legacy Outlook. Accounts added in one client are not automatically added to the other, so check which accounts you see after any switch.

Microsoft's support page says support for legacy Outlook for Mac ends in October 2026. It gives no exact day. Continued support depends on your Microsoft 365, Office, or Outlook license. October 2026 has already passed, so ask your IT admin which client your account should use.

blocks.title: Do not guess the client
blocks.text: Some blog posts give a specific legacy end date. Follow Microsoft's wording and your IT admin's notice. A guide written for one client may show menus that do not match the other.
Excel for HR trackers: working days, dates, and lookups

Many HR generalists keep leave, training, or onboarding trackers in Excel. The most common snag is counting working days between two dates. NETWORKDAYS counts weekdays between two dates and skips any holidays you list. It includes both the start and end dates.

Here is a worked example. Leave runs from Monday 2 November 2026 to Friday 13 November 2026. That is 10 working days. Add a holiday on Wednesday 4 November, and the count drops to 9. The formula is =NETWORKDAYS(B2,C2,Holidays), where B2 is the start, C2 is the end, and Holidays is your holiday range.

items: Dates stored as text. Excel will not count text as dates. Check that the cells are real dates before you write the formula.
A holiday range that includes the header. Point the formula at the dates only.
Forgetting that both ends count. A one-day leave on a weekday should return 1.
Fixing a messy list with a pivot table. Clean the list first, then follow the pivot table guide.

blocks.text: Ask Lazur to explain the formula before you copy it. Hold Option and Command on the sheet and ask what each part does. Then type it yourself. For a full walk through summaries, read the [pivot table guide](/how-to/make-a-pivot-table-in-excel) and the [Excel page for HR generalists](/for/hr-generalists/excel).
AI tools and employee data: your duties come first

Employee records are personal data. Your employer decides what can go into an AI tool. Ask your privacy or legal contact before you use any AI tool with names, health details, pay, or disciplinary notes. Do not assume a tool is safe because it runs on your Mac.

Here is what Lazur does with your screen. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Those are product facts, not a substitute for your company's policy.

blocks.title: Clear the screen first
blocks.text: Lazur looks at what is on screen when you hold the shortcut. Close or minimize any record you do not need for the question. Then hold Option and Command.

Research has limits too. Lazur can gather public sources and report back, but it does not give legal advice. For questions about leave, discipline, or pay, your employment counsel decides what applies to your company.
A worked example: answering a leave question in Slack
A manager posts in Slack asking whether an employee can take three weeks of unpaid leave. You need the policy, a reply, and a note for the file. Here is one way to handle it with Lazur.

items: Open the message. If you missed it, follow the [Slack unread steps](/how-to/jump-to-the-latest-unread-message-in-slack).
Put the leave policy page on screen, then hold Option and Command and ask what it says about unpaid leave. Lazur answers out loud.
Hold fn and dictate the outcome you want to give the manager.
Ask Lazur to draft a short reply that cites the policy section. You fix the names and dates.
Reply in the thread. The [thread guide](/how-to/reply-in-a-thread-in-slack) shows the steps if you need them.

blocks.text: If the request involves health details, move that detail to a private message or your HR system. Your policy decides where those details belong.
Mistakes that cost HR generalists time

items: Asking for legal answers. Lazur explains and drafts. It does not replace counsel.
Pasting whole files at once. Ask about one row, one clause, or one thread at a time.
Sending a draft without reading it. Check names, dates, and amounts every time.
Holding the shortcut with the wrong window open. Lazur answers from what is on screen.
Following an Outlook guide written for the other client. Confirm which client you use first.

faq.question: Can Lazur type into my Excel sheet or send my email for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not operate other apps for you. It points, guides, explains, and drafts text. You type the formula, edit the draft, and press Send yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur run inside Excel, Gmail, or Outlook?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a separate voice assistant on your Mac. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. It works with what is on your screen.

faq.question: Can I paste employee records into Lazur?
faq.answer: Check with your employer first. Employee records are personal data, and your company decides what can go into an AI tool. Lazur sends audio and screenshots to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur is for macOS on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: How much does the trial cost?
faq.answer: Nothing up front. The 3-day Pro trial needs no credit card and starts the first time you open the app. Pro is $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually, with 250 AI actions.

faq.question: Can Lazur answer legal questions about leave, discipline, or pay?
faq.answer: It can explain what is on your screen and gather public sources. It does not give legal advice. Take questions about leave, discipline, or pay to your employment counsel or legal contact.

faq.question: Will Lazur work with Outlook for Mac after the client switch?
faq.answer: Lazur works with what is on your screen in any app. Check which Outlook client your account supports first. Microsoft's support page says legacy support ends in October 2026, depending on your license.

demo.spoken: Lazur, how do I count working days between these two dates?
demo.context: Leave tracker in Excel for Microsoft 365 on Mac. Start date in column B, end date in column C, holidays on another sheet.
demo.output: Put this in D2: =NETWORKDAYS(B2,C2,Holidays). B2 is the start date and C2 is the end date. Holidays is a range that lists your holiday dates. If you have none, leave that part out and the formula still works. Type it in the formula bar, press Return, then copy the formula down the column.
demo.result: Lazur points at cell D2 and reads the formula out loud. You type it into the formula bar, and the row shows 10 for 2 to 13 November 2026.
